rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads the listed passive forms with initial ḍamma, including qīla and jīʾa.
rows.anchor: قرأ الكسائي قيل وغيض وسئ وسيئت وحيل وسيق وجيء بضم أوائل ذلك كله

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb is also reported to use the initial-ḍamma reading for all these forms.
rows.anchor: وروي عن يعقوب مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ agrees with the preceding reading for سيء and سيئت.
rows.anchor: ووافقهما نافع في سيء وسيئت

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir agrees for سيء, سيئت, حيل, and سيق.
rows.anchor: وابن عامر فيهما وفي حيل وسيق

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers use kasra throughout the listed forms.
rows.anchor: والباقون يكسون كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive forms have three linguistic realizations: kasra, a hint of ḍamma, and a waw-based form; qīla derives by moving the vowel and changing wāw to yāʾ.
rows.anchor: في هذه كلها ثلاث لغات الكسر وإشمام الضم وقول بالواو فأما قيل بالكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hint of ḍamma preserves a trace of the original form while easing pronunciation.
rows.anchor: وأما الإشمام فلأجل الدلالة على الأصل مع التخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فساد means causing corruption, any departure from sound order; ṣalāḥ is its opposite, and earth is where animals settle, also reflected in the cited horse verse.
rows.anchor: الإفساد إحداث الفساد وهو كل ما تغير عن استقامة الحال والصلاح نقيض الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذا is temporal and conditional; it functions as an adverb, and its answer governs it rather than the quoted response verb itself.
rows.anchor: إذا لفظة وضعت للوقت بشرط أن يكون ظرفا زمانيا وفيها معنى الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In وإذا لقوا, إذا is built because it carries the meaning of في and adheres to it; it can also be spatial, as in خرجت فإذا الناس وقوف.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قوله: وإذا لقوا الذين آمنوا قالوا آمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression إنما makes إن non-governing, leaving نحن مبتدأ and مصلحون its predicate; نحن is built like a particle and marked by ḍamma as a plural nominative pronoun.
rows.anchor: وما في قوله إنما كافة كفت إن عن العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause لا تفسدوا في الأرض is parsed as a raised clause understood as something said to them.
rows.anchor: جملة في موضع رفع على تقدير قيل لهم شيء فهي اسم ما لم يسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إلا introduces and opens a self-sufficient statement; it began as لا preceded by interrogative alif, which turns denial into confirmation.
rows.anchor: إلا كلمة تنبيه وافتتاح للكلام تدخل على كل كلام مكتف بنفسه

rows.speaker: بعض القراء
rows.claim: Some readers omit the hamza in مستهزؤون.
rows.anchor: بعض القراء ترك الهمزة من مستهزؤون

rows.speaker: أهل الحجاز
rows.claim: The Hijazi reading of خلوا إلى drops the hamza and transfers its vowel to the preceding wāw.
rows.anchor: قراءة أهل الحجاز خلولى حذفوا الهمزة وألقوا حركتها على الواو قبلها

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers leave the wāw unvowelled and pronounce the hamza fully.
rows.anchor: والباقون أسكنوا الواو وحققوا الهمزة

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh says a hamza may be softened to an intermediate sound in the cited vowel environments.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه: الهمزة المضمومة المكسور ما قبلها تجعلها إذا خففتها بين بين

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash instead fully changes the hamza of مستهزيون to yāʾ because of the preceding kasra; he rejects intermediate treatment or wāw because they yield an unparalleled form.
rows.anchor: وذهب الأخفش إلى أن تقلب الهمزة ياء في مستهزيون قلبا صحيحا

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl defines meeting as anything encountering or coming across something, originally coming together by proximity.
rows.anchor: قال الخليل: كل شيء استقبل شيئا أو صادفه فقد لقيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خلوت إليه and خلوت معه mean being alone with someone; خلوت به can also mean mocking him.
rows.anchor: ويقال خلوت إليه وخلوت معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يستهزئون means they mock; the same verb-pattern shifts meaning in examples such as يستسخرون, يستقر, and استعلى قرنه.
rows.anchor: ويستهزئون أي يهزءون ومثله يستسخرون أي يسخرون وقر واستقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنا is shortened from إننا by dropping the second nūn; معكم is adverbial, meaning settled with you.
rows.anchor: إنا أصله إننا لكن النون حذفت لكثرة النونات والمحذوفة النون الثانية من إن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative construction is illustrated by the poet's expression وريشي منكم وهواي معكم.
rows.anchor: انتصب انتصاب الظروف نحو إنا خلفكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites tell believers that they believe what was sent to Muhammad, then tell their leaders privately that they share their religion and only mock Muhammad's companions.
rows.anchor: أن المنافقين إذا رأوا المؤمنين قالوا آمنا أي صدقنا نحن بما أنزل على محمد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the hypocrites' shayāṭīn as their unbelieving leaders.
rows.anchor: قيل رؤساؤهم من الكفار عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported view identifies the shayāṭīn as Jews who instructed the hypocrites to deny the message.
rows.anchor: وقيل هم اليهود الذين أمروهم بالتكذيب

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر الباقر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir says the shayāṭīn are their soothsayers.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي جعفر الباقر عليه السلام أنهم كهانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنما نحن مستهزئون means they claim to be with their leaders in religion and to mock and ridicule Muhammad's companions when professing faith.
rows.anchor: أي على دينكم إنما نحن مستهزءون أي نستهزئ بأصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: جميع القراء
rows.claim: All canonical readers put ḍamma on the wāw of اشتروا.
rows.anchor: قرأ جميع القراء اشتروا الضلالة بضم الواو

rows.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: In a noncanonical reading, Yaḥyā b. Yaʿmar gives the wāw kasra by analogy with the wāw in لو.
rows.anchor: وفي الشواذ عن يحيى بن يعمر أنه كسرها تشبيها بواو لو

rows.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
rows.claim: Yaḥyā b. Waththāb is reported to give the wāw of لو ḍamma by analogy with the plural wāw.
rows.anchor: وروي عن يحيى بن وثاب أنه ضم واو لو تشبيها بواو الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw is vowelled after dropping the alif of the article brings two sukūns together; ḍamma distinguishes it from لو and أو and signals plurality.
rows.anchor: فحرك الأول منهما لالتقائهما وصار الضم أولى بها ليفصل بالضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analogy among wāw forms is like analogical case alternations in الضارب الرجل and الحسن الوجه.
rows.anchor: ومثل هذا إجازتهم الجر في الضارب الرجل تشبيها بالحسن الوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purchase means exchange; Arabs also call choosing and holding one thing while leaving another a purchase, as the cited poem shows.
rows.anchor: حقيقة الاشتراء الاستبدال والعرب تقول لمن تمسك بشيء وترك غيره قد اشتراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Profit is growth over capital; trade is seeking profit through sale, and Arabic may attribute profit or loss directly to the sale or trade.
rows.anchor: والتجارة التعرض للربح في البيع وقوله فما ربحت تجارتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أولئك begins the sentence, while الذين اشتروا is its predicate; with كان, مهتدين is its predicate and the plural ending derives historically from مهتديين.
rows.anchor: أولئك موضعه رفع بالابتداء وخبره الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كان may denote only time and require a predicate, or be a full verb denoting both time and an event, as in the cited 2:282 phrase.
rows.anchor: والآخر من نحوى كان ما هو فعل حقيقي يدل على زمان وحدث

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the exchange as taking misguidance and abandoning guidance, meaning replacing faith with unbelief.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس أخذوا الضلالة وتركوا الهدى ومعناه استبدلوا الكفر بالإيمان

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says they preferred and chose misguidance, since a buyer prefers what the other party holds.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that they were born on the primordial disposition and then left it for unbelief, as the report says.
rows.anchor: أنهم ولدوا على الفطرة كما جاء في الخبر فتركوا ذلك إلى الكفر

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil say they had believed in and expected Muhammad before his mission, then exchanged that faith for unbelief when he was sent.
rows.anchor: عن الكلبي ومقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their trade failed: they replaced faith with unbelief and reward with punishment, and were not rightly guided as Muhammad's companions were.
rows.anchor: أي خسروا في استبدالهم الكفر بالإيمان والعذاب بالثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading takes the verse as denying them both profit and guidance, since a trader can lose while still being guided.
rows.anchor: فإن التاجر قد يخسر ولا يربح ويكون على هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of profit contrasts the exchange of misguidance for guidance with believers' profitable exchange of guidance for misguidance; in substance the hypocrites lose their capital.
rows.anchor: طلبوا الربح فلم يربحوا وهلكوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نقض is the opposite of confirming a bond; عهد can mean a covenant, binding pledge, or God's command and instruction.
rows.anchor: النقض نقيض الإبرام والعهد العقد والعهد الموثق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A covenant is God's instruction, as in the address ألم أعهد إليكم بني آدم.
rows.anchor: وعهد الله وصيته وأمره يقال عهد الخليفة إلى فلان بكذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mīthāq is the thing by which a pledge is made binding; qaṭʿ originally divides physical things and extends metaphorically to speech and matters.
rows.anchor: والميثاق ما وقع التوثيق به كما أن الميقات ما وقع التوقيت به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command form fundamentally requests action, though it can express permission, threat, challenge, or creative fiat.
rows.anchor: والأصل في الجميع الطلب والوصل نقيض الفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Loss is diminution or destruction, and the root idea is losing one's capital.
rows.anchor: وأصل الخسران ذهاب رأس المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الذين ينقضون is an accusative adjective describing the previously mentioned evildoers; أولئك begins the next clause and الخاسرون is its predicate.
rows.anchor: الذين ينقضون في موضع النصب لأنها صفة الفاسقين وأولئك مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The min in من بعد may be extra or mark a starting point; the suffix in ميثاقه may refer to the covenant or to God.
rows.anchor: من مزيدة وقيل معناه ابتداء الغاية والهاء في ميثاقه عائد إلى العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase أن يوصل appositionally explains the pronoun in به: what God commanded to be joined.
rows.anchor: أن يوصل بدل من الهاء التي في به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes the covenant as rational evidence for divine unity and justice and prophetic proofs; breaking it means refusing what reason showed to be true.
rows.anchor: أنه ركب في عقولهم من أدلة التوحيد والعدل وتصديق الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view understands God's covenant as the commands and prohibitions delivered by His messenger; breaking it means failing to act on them.
rows.anchor: أنه وصية الله إلى خلقه على لسان رسوله بما أمرهم به من طاعته

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the view that the covenant was the People of the Book's pledge in the Torah to follow Muhammad and disclose the truth, which they knowingly concealed.
rows.anchor: واختار هذا الوجه الطبري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The view that the covenant was taken when humanity was brought from Adam's loins is weak: God cannot bind people by an unknown pledge without evidence.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه ضعيف لأنه لا يجوز أن يحتج على عباده بعهد لا يذكرونه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the severed relationship is ties with the Prophet and believers, whom the breakers were ordered to maintain.
rows.anchor: أمروا بصلة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمؤمنين فقطعوهم عن الحسن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says it is kinship and family ties that they were commanded to keep.
rows.anchor: أمروا بصلة الرحم والقرابة فقطعوها عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views understand the severed command as belief in all prophets and scriptures, or as joining words to deeds rather than professing without acting.
rows.anchor: وقيل أمروا بالإيمان بجميع الأنبياء والكتب ففرقوا وقطعوا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The broadest interpretation is to include everyone God commands people to join among His allies; cutting them off means repudiating and rejecting them.
rows.anchor: وهذا أقوى لأنه أعم ويدخل فيه الجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Corruption on earth has been explained as calling people to unbelief, frightening travelers and blocking roads, or breaking God's covenant.
rows.anchor: قال قوم استدعاؤهم إلى الكفر هو الفساد في الأرض وقيل إخافتهم السبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best reading generalizes corruption to every sin whose harm extends beyond its perpetrator; the breakers destroy themselves and lose their capital.
rows.anchor: أي اهلكوا أنفسهم فهم بمنزلة من هلك رأس ماله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says loss attributed to non-Muslims means unbelief, while loss attributed to Muslims means worldly loss.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أن كل ما نسبه الله تعالى من الخسار إلى غير المسلمين

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة والشام
rows.claim: The Medinan and Syrian readers use وأوصى with hamza and a light ṣād.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة والشام وأوصى بهمزة بين واوين وتخفيف الصاد

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers use ووصى with a doubled ṣād.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون ووصى مشددة الصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubled form is supported by توصية as the verbal noun of وصى; a doubled form here would produce an impermissible cluster of three yāʾs.
rows.anchor: فتوصية مصدر وصى مثل قطع تقطعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza reading is supported by God's wording يوصيكم الله and من بعد وصية توصون بها.
rows.anchor: حجة من قرأ وأوصى بها إبراهيم قوله يوصيكم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وصى and أوصى mean the same as command and charge; the root also describes joined parts of a house.
rows.anchor: وصى وأوصى وأمر وعهد بمعنى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda parse Jacob as coordinated with Abraham: both charged their sons with this faith.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن عباس وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordination with Abraham is clearer because it requires no omitted words; the alternative treats Jacob as beginning a new clause with an implied charge.
rows.anchor: والأول أظهر والفرق بين التقديرين أن الأول لا إضمار فيه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the pronoun in بها refers to the milla, while another view takes it to refer to the statement أسلمت لرب العالمين.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الزجاج وقيل إنها تعود إلى الكلمة التي هي أسلمت لرب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite expression الدين refers specifically to the known religion of Islam, not religion in general.
rows.anchor: والألف واللام في الدين للعهد دون الاستغراق لأنه أراد دين الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition against dying except as Muslims actually commands them not to abandon Islam, so death will find them adhering to it; Arabic لا أرينك here has the same indirect force.
rows.anchor: فالنهي على الحقيقة عن ترك الإسلام لئلا يصادفهم الموت عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase بها may refer to the enduring word of monotheism, as supported by the statement that God made it a lasting word, or to the declaration of faith لا إله إلا الله.
rows.anchor: وقيل بكلمة الإخلاص وهي لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim addressed his sons because his concern for them was greater and they were especially likely to accept his charge, although he called all people to Islam.
rows.anchor: إنما خص البنين لأن إشفاقه عليهم أكثر وهم بقبول وصيته أجدر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Jacob, son of Isaac, was named Yaʿqūb because his twin ʿĪṣ preceded him at birth and Yaʿqūb followed holding his heel.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس والمعنى ووصى يعقوب بنيه الاثني عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob charged his twelve sons, the tribes, that God had chosen Islam for them.
rows.anchor: والمعنى ووصى يعقوب بنيه الاثني عشر وهم الأسباط

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the instruction as remaining committed to Islam so that death finds them Muslim.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج معناه الزموا الإسلام فإذا أدرككم الموت صادفكم مسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse encourages a person approaching death to instruct dependents to fear God and keep to religion and obedience.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على الترغيب في الوصية عند الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnesses are those present; the root denotes presence as opposed to absence and yields related words for gatherings, racing, and a person's courtyard.
rows.anchor: وأصل الباب الحضور خلاف الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أم is discontinuous, meaning بل plus a question, while the sense is denial: the addressees were not witnesses; the interrogative form makes the proof more forceful.
rows.anchor: أم ها هنا منقطعة وهي لا تجيء إلا وقد تقدمها كلام لأنها التي تكون بمعنى بل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first إذا is governed by شهداء, while the second may be governed by حضر; either parsing is valid.
rows.anchor: وإذ الأولى ظرف من قوله شهداء وإذ الثانية بدل من إذ الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إلها واحدا may be a circumstantial phrase or apposition to إلهك; ونحن له مسلمون may likewise be circumstantial or a fresh sentence.
rows.anchor: منصوب على أحد وجهين أن يكون حالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patriarch names are genitive appositions to آبائك.
rows.anchor: في موضع جر على البدل من آبائك كما تقول مررت بالقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing the People of the Book, God denies they witnessed Jacob's deathbed and rejects claims that the prophets were Jews or Christians; Jacob commended pure monotheism, not Judaism.
rows.anchor: فلا تدعوا على أنبيائي ورسلي الأباطيل بأن تنسبوهم إلى اليهودية والنصرانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks what they will worship, rather than whom, because people then worshipped idols.
rows.anchor: لأن الناس كانوا يعبدون الأصنام فقال أي الأشياء تعبدون من بعدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael is named before Isaac because he was older; although Jacob's uncle, Ishmael is called his father as Arabs also call an uncle a father, due the honor owed him.
rows.anchor: وإنما قدم ذكر إسماعيل على إسحاق لأنه كان أكبر منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Arabic calls Jacob’s uncle Ishmael a father because uncles and grandfathers receive a father’s honor, then introduces a Prophetic report supporting the usage.
rows.anchor: وإسماعيل كان عم يعقوب وجعله أبا له لأن العرب تسمي العم أبا كما تسمي الجد أبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were submissive, acknowledging servitude; another explanation emphasizes humility and surrender in belief and practice.
rows.anchor: أي مذعنون مقرون بالعبودية وقيل خاضعون منقادون مستسلمون لأمره ونهيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation takes مسلمون to mean that they entered Islam, supported by the verse saying God's religion is Islam.
rows.anchor: وقيل داخلون في الإسلام يدل عليه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما أصبرهم may be an exclamation like the wording in 80:17, meaning they have become an object of astonishment; an Arab saying likewise describes one as patient toward God's punishment.
rows.anchor: ما أصبرهم قيل إن للتعجب كالتي في قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase asks what makes them endure the Fire; the verb can mean to subject someone to what they dislike, as in al-Ḥuṭayʾa's poem.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه للاستفهام على معنى أي شيء أصبرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refers back to those who traded misguidance for guidance, replacing belief in the Prophet with unbelief.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى من تقدم ذكرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations take misguidance as concealing what they knew about the Prophet, or as punishment exchanged for reward and Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد الضلالة كتمان أمره مع علمهم به وبالهدى إظهاره

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim considers “exchanging punishment for forgiveness” a reinforcement of the preceding exchange.
rows.anchor: قيل إنه تأكيد لما تقدم عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī says they knowingly exchanged forgiveness for punishment by persisting in disobedience; al-Ṭabrisī prefers this because it adds a distinct meaning.
rows.anchor: عن القاضي وهذا أولى لأنه إذا أمكن حمل الكلام على زيادة فائدة كان أولى

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda take فما أصبرهم as “how audacious they are toward the Fire.”
rows.anchor: ما أجرأهم على النار ذهب إليه الحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets it as “how active they are in deeds of the people of the Fire.”
rows.anchor: ما أعملهم بأعمال أهل النار عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj understands the phrase as how long they remain in the Fire, like asking how long someone can endure prison.
rows.anchor: ما أبقاهم على النار كما يقال ما أصبر فلانا على الحبس عن الزجاج

rows.speaker: الكسائي وقطرب
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and Quṭrub read it as how persistent they are in deeds leading to the Fire.
rows.anchor: ما أدومهم على النار أي ما أدومهم على عمل أهل النار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the wording as an actual question: what keeps them confined to the Fire?
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن المراد أي شيء أصبرهم على النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Literal divine astonishment is impossible because God knows everything; the exclamation instead makes the unbelievers an object of human amazement, rebuke, and reproach, while the readings can also be understood interrogatively.
rows.anchor: والتعجب لا يجوز على القديم سبحانه لأنه عالم بجميع الأشياء لا يخفى عليه شيء

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad calls the interrogative reading a good rebuke that makes people marvel at those who freely bring ruin on themselves.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد هذا حسن لأنه كالتوبيخ لهم والتعجب لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Burūz is appearing into open view; afrāgh is pouring liquid so as to empty a vessel, and تثبيت makes something firm in its place.
rows.anchor: والإفراغ الصب للسيال على جهة إخلاء المكان منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Victory is aid against an enemy through increased strength, fear, exposure of weakness, imagined numbers, or division; divine victory is always لطف, though not every لطف is victory.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين النصر واللطف أن كل نصر من الله فهو لطف وليس كل لطف نصرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience is the servant's restraint from an urged action, here restraint from fleeing combat, and it is rewarded.
rows.anchor: والصبر من فعل العبد لأنه يجازي عليه وهو حبس النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Ṭālūt's believers faced Jālūt, they asked God to grant full patience, likened to pouring all a vessel holds, and to enable steadfastness and victory in jihad.
rows.anchor: أي وفقنا للصبر على الجهاد وشبهه بتفريغ الإناء

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamza alone reads إن تضل with kasra, as a conditional particle whose جواب is فتذكر.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة وحده إن تضل بكسر الهمزة

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وقتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and Qutayba read فتذكر lightly and in the subjunctive.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وقتيبة فتذكر بالتخفيف والنصب

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads فتذكر with doubled dhāl and indicative mood.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة فتذكر بالتشديد والرفع

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers read فتذكر with doubled dhāl and subjunctive mood.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون فتذكر بالتشديد والنصب

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim alone reads تجارة حاضرة in the accusative; the others read it nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحده تجارة حاضرة بالنصب

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads لا يضار with a doubled, quiescent rāʾ; the remaining readers use the doubled rāʾ in the accusative form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ولا يضار بتشديد الراء وتسكينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Ḥamza's conditional reading, رجل وامرأتان forms a nominative description of the two women, while ممن ترضون refers back to that nominative pair rather than accusative شهيدين.
rows.anchor: وهو أنه جعل أن للجزاء والفاء في قوله فتذكر جواب الجزاء

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: A third analysis supplies an omitted predicate for the subject فرجل وامرأتان, understood as فرجل وامرأتان يشهدون.
rows.anchor: والثالث: أن يضمر خبر المبتدأ الذي هو فرجل وامرأتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this analysis يشهدون governs أن; its omission is placed before the conditional with fatḥ and after it with kasra.
rows.anchor: فيكون يشهدون العامل في أن وموضع إضماره فيمن فتح الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle أن is accusative here, with the sense “because one woman may forget, then the other remind her.”
rows.anchor: وأما موضع أن هذه فنصب وتقديره لأن تضل إحداهما فتذكر

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh says testimony is requested so one woman may remind the other; possible forgetfulness is the reason for reminding, like shoring a wall because it may lean.
rows.anchor: أمر بالإشهاد لأن تذكر إحداهما الأخرى وإنما ذكر أن تضل لأنه سبب الأذكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the nominative reading, كان means “occur” or “happen,” so the phrase means that a present trade occurs.
rows.anchor: بالرفع فالوجه فيها أن يكون كان بمعنى وقع وحدث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis derives لا يضار from doubled ر, with the writer and witness forbidden to depart from the truth.
rows.anchor: أن أصله لا يضارر فادغمت الراء في الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first interpretation of لا يضار is clearer; Abū Jaʿfar's doubled quiescent rāʾ is unusual and explained by treating connected recitation like pause.
rows.anchor: والأول أبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: داينت and تداينت mean transacting in debt, either by borrowing or lending; the cited poem shows this usage.
rows.anchor: داينت أروى والديون تقضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb دنت means borrowing while أدنت means lending; أمل and أملى are both used for dictating.
rows.anchor: ويقال دنت وأدنت إذا اقترضت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بخس is unjust diminution; safīh means ignorant or light-minded, named for the lightness of reason.
rows.anchor: والبخس النقص ظلما يقال بخسه حقه يبخسه بخسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The otherwise unusual pattern أَبَى يَأبى is explained by the hamza behaving like a guttural consonant.
rows.anchor: والقول فيه أن الألف من أبى أشبهت الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍalāl originally means loss or going where something cannot be found; saʾam is weariness, and أقسط means acted justly while قسط means acted unjustly.
rows.anchor: والضلال أصله الهلاك تقول العرب ضل الماء في اللبن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening continues the previous direction to defer an insolvent debtor by explaining rules for deferred claims and debt transactions.
rows.anchor: لما أمر سبحانه بإنظار المعسر وتأجيل دينه عقبه ببيان أحكام الحقوق المؤجلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بدين may reinforce the meaning of تداينتم; alternatively it distinguishes debt transactions from تداينتم understood as mutual requital.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أنه على وجه التأكيد وتمكين المعنى في النفسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis takes تداينتم as mutual requital, while another takes it as dealing in debt; adding بدين resolves this lexical ambiguity.
rows.anchor: إنما قال بدين لأن تداينتم قد يكون بمعنى تجازيتم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed specifically concerning forward sale and testifies that God permitted a guaranteed sale to a known term.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إن الآية وردت في السلم خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Ibn ʿAbbās specifies forward sale, the verse's apparent scope includes every deferred debt, which commentators and jurists accept.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآية يقع على كل دين مؤجل سلما كان أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing the debt protects against forgetting or denial and secures the rights of creditor, debtor, and witnesses for the reasons explained.
rows.anchor: فاكتبوا الدين في صك لئلا يقع فيه نسيان أو جحود وليكون ذلك توثقة للحق

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري والحسن والشعبي
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, al-Ḥasan, and al-Shaʿbī say writing the debt is recommended, the majority's preferred view.
rows.anchor: مندوب إليه عن أبي سعيد الخدري والحسن والشعبي وهو الأصح

rows.speaker: الربيع وكعب
rows.claim: Al-Rabīʿ and Kaʿb regard writing as obligatory; the author cites the permission to rely on trust as evidence against obligation.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو فرض عن الربيع وكعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A just scribe records the debt or sale accurately, without changing its terms, amount, or anything that harms either party without consent.
rows.anchor: بالقسط والإنصاف والحق لا يزيد فيه ولا ينقص منه في صفة ولا مقدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scribe must not refuse to write; كما علمه الله may mean writing justly as God taught, or that the scribe must not hoard the skill God gave him.
rows.anchor: وقيل كما فضله الله تعالى بتعليمه إياه فلا يبخل على غيره بالكتابة

rows.speaker: الشعبي وجماعة من المفسرين
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī and other commentators treat writing as a communal duty; al-Rummānī and al-Jubbāʾī choose that view.
rows.anchor: فقيل على الكفاية كالجهاد ونحوه عن الشعبي وجماعة من المفسرين

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī allows a scribe and witness to take payment, while al-Ṭūsī says their school does not permit it; paper costs belong to the creditor.
rows.anchor: وجوز الجبائي أن يأخذ الكاتب والشاهد الأجرة على ذلك

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says a scribe must write when free of other work.
rows.anchor: وقيل واجب على الكاتب أن يكتب في حال فراغه عن السدي

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء
rows.claim: Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ say writing becomes obligatory when the scribe is asked.
rows.anchor: وقيل واجب عليه أن يكتب إذا أمر عن مجاهد وعطاء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says refusal is obligatory to avoid only when there is no alternative scribe and refusal would harm the creditor; otherwise the scribe has latitude.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان كذلك فهو فريضة وإن قدر على كاتب غيره فهو في سعة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says writing was originally obligatory but was abrogated by the ban on harming a scribe or witness.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان واجبا ثم نسخ بقوله ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is emphasized because scribes were scarce in the Prophet's time; combining a command with a prohibition against neglect makes compliance more likely.
rows.anchor: وكانت الكتبة على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيهم قلة فلذلك أكد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debtor dictates and must fear God, reducing neither the amount nor the quality of what is owed.
rows.anchor: يعني المديون يقر على نفسه بلسانه ليعلم ما عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debtor may be a fool through ignorance, childhood, or impaired understanding; weak may mean intellectual disability or senility, and inability may mean madness, stammering, or muteness.
rows.anchor: أي جاهلا بالإملاء عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī differentiates the three: the foolish person squanders, the weak person is an adolescent, and the one unable to dictate is insane.
rows.anchor: السفيه المبذر والضعيف الصبي المراهق ومن لا يستطيع أن يمل المجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debtor's guardian may dictate; alternatively, Ibn ʿAbbās says the guardian here is the creditor, who knows the debt best.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه ولي الحق وهو الذي له الحق عن ابن عباس لأنه أعلم بدينه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid limits the two male witnesses to free, adult, Muslim men; al-Ṭabrisī rejects freedom as a condition, requiring Islam and probity instead.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: معناه من الأحرار العالمين البالغين المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If two men are unavailable, the witness set is one man and two women whose outward probity and trustworthiness the parties accept; this makes justice a condition of testimony.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن العدالة شرط في الشهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording requires witnesses acceptable to the parties, since people cannot know whom God approves except from outward reliability and integrity.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل من المرضيين لأنه لا طريق لنا إلى معرفة من هو مرضي عند الله

rows.speaker: الربيع والسدي والضحاك وأكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators take تضل as one woman forgetting the testimony she and the other woman heard; the light reading likewise means prompting her to recall it.
rows.anchor: قيل هو من الذكر الذي هو ضد النسيان عن الربيع والسدي والضحاك

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyān b. ʿUyayna reads the doubled form as making one woman equivalent to a man; al-Ṭabrisī says the memory-based reading is stronger.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو من الذكر أي يجعلها كذكر من الرجال عن سفيان بن عيينة

rows.speaker: حسين بن علي المغربي
rows.claim: Al-Maghribī says تضل concerns a lost or forgotten testimony, not a woman herself going astray; this avoids needless repetition of إحداهما.
rows.anchor: ما قاله حسين بن علي المغربي أن معناه أن تضل إحدى الشهادتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated إحداهما may put the subject before its object and avoid separating verb and subject, or may clarify that a testimony is lost rather than a person straying.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أنه إنما كرر ليكون الفاعل مقدما على المفعول

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: One reported view says summoned witnesses must not refuse to give testimony they know without doubt, provided doing so causes them no harm.
rows.anchor: ولا يمتنع الشهداء إذا دعوا لإقامة الشهادة عن مجاهد وعطاء وسعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: قتادة والربيع
rows.claim: Qatāda and al-Rabīʿ say the witnesses must not refuse when summoned to establish and carry the testimony.
rows.anchor: أن معناه إذا دعوا لاثبات الشهادة وتحملها عن قتادة والربيع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan understand the summons as covering both bearing and delivering testimony; the author prefers this broader reading.
rows.anchor: وهو أولى لأنه أعم فائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not weary of recording a debt, small or large, until its term; this is fairer, steadier testimony, and less likely to leave doubts about amount or term.
rows.anchor: أي ولا تضجروا ولا تملوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command may address witnesses and mean not to tire of recording testimony; the stronger referent of its term is the debt's due date, not the witness's allowable period.
rows.anchor: أي إلى أجل الدين وقيل معناه إلى أجل الشاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing the debt or testimony is more just before God, more reliable for testimony, and closer to preventing doubt; قسط means fairness and الأقسط means acting justly.
rows.anchor: اتباع أمره أعدل من تركه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A spot transaction exchanged hand to hand can be left unwritten because documentation is needed for deferred payment, not cash trade.
rows.anchor: فليس عليكم إثم في ترك كتابتها لأن الكتابة للوثيقة

rows.speaker: الحسن وجميع الفقهاء
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and the jurists regard witnessing sales as recommended; the Ẓāhirīs make it obligatory.
rows.anchor: وهذا أمر على الاستحباب والندب عن الحسن وجميع الفقهاء

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وعطاء وابن زيد
rows.claim: With kasra on the first rāʾ, the prohibition addresses the writer and witness: do not change dictated terms, testify to matters not requested, or refuse to testify.
rows.anchor: أصله يضارر بكسر الراء الأولى عن الحسن وقتادة وعطاء وابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود ومجاهد
rows.claim: With fatḥ on the first rāʾ, the prohibition tells people not to impose writing on a busy scribe or summon a witness when excused, or to mistreat either.
rows.anchor: وقيل الأصل فيه لا يضارر بفتح الراء الأولى عن ابن مسعود ومجاهد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the first reading is clearer because deliberate falsification makes someone a wrongdoer more plausibly than summoning a busy witness does.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج والأول أبين لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse threatens that harming a scribe or witness in writing or testimony is a departure from God's commands; fear God, who teaches what is needed and knows all.
rows.anchor: معناه وإن تفعلوا مضارة الكاتب والشهيد فإن المضارة في الكتابة والشهادة فسوق بكم

rows.speaker: علي بن إبراهيم بن هاشم
rows.claim: ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm b. Hāshim's tafsīr counts five hundred legal rulings in al-Baqara and fifteen in this verse alone.
rows.anchor: وذكر علي بن إبراهيم بن هاشم في تفسيره أن في البقرة خمسمائة حكم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read رهن as faʿl; the other readers read رهٰان on the faʿāl pattern.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو فرهن على وزن فعل والباقون فرهان على وزن فعال

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says رهن began as a verbal noun, became a noun by transfer, and is pluralized on both فعْل and فعال patterns; the cited verse attests the form.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: الرهن مصدر ولما نقل فسمي به كسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root رهن means placing property as security; a pledge may also be called a mortgage, with related alternative forms and expressions for advancing or maintaining food.
rows.anchor: يقال رهنت عند الرجل رهنا ورهنته رهنا وأنا أرهنه

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says the reading أرهنتهم مالكا in Ibn Hammām's verse is mistaken; the correct wording is وأرهنهم مالكا.
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي من روي بيت ابن همام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophetic rule لا يغلق الرهن invalidates a condition that if the borrower does not redeem by a set date the collateral becomes the creditor's property.
rows.anchor: " لا يغلق الرهن " فمعناه أن يقول الراهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When debtors travel without a scribe or witnesses, a received pledge serves as security and is valid only upon possession, by consensus.
rows.anchor: والقبض شرط في صحة الرهن فإن لم يقبض لم ينعقد الرهن بالاجماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the creditor trusts the debtor without a written or pledged security, the debtor must fully repay at maturity without denial or delay.
rows.anchor: بأن لا يجحد حقه ولا يبخس منه شيئا ويؤديه إليه وافيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order not to conceal testimony addresses witnesses after they have borne it; intentional concealment by one who knows the fact and can testify without harm makes the heart sinful.
rows.anchor: يعني بعد تحملها وهو خطاب للشهود ونهي لهم عن كتمان الشهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sin is assigned to the heart because the decision to conceal is made there, and this wording intensifies blame; the verse on faith in hearts provides a parallel.
rows.anchor: لأن اكتساب الإثم بكتمان الشهادة يقع بالقلب لأن العزم على الكتمان إنما يقع بالقلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what people conceal; a report from the Prophet says a false witness leaves the judge only after taking his seat in Hell, as does one who hides testimony.
rows.anchor: لا ينقضي كلام شاهد زور من بين يدي الحاكم حتى يتبوأ مقعده من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause permitting trust between the parties shows that writing and witnesses in debt transactions are safeguards, not obligations.
rows.anchor: دلالة على أن الاشهاد والكتابة في المداينة ليسا بواجبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two verses show God's care in teaching people what they need for worldly and religious life, offering insight to the reflective.
rows.anchor: وتضمنت هذه الآية وما قبلها من بدائع لطف الله تعالى ونظره لعباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribāṭ originally meant tethering horses against an enemy, then came to mean staying at a frontier post to defend those behind; it also names the tether itself.
rows.anchor: أصل الرباط ارتباط الخيل للعدو والربط الشد ومنه قولهم ربط الله على قلبه

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن جريج والضحاك
rows.claim: They explain the commands as remaining firm in religion, persevering against unbelievers, and guarding the frontier; this means obeying God, avoiding sin, and enduring combat as the enemy does.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن وقتادة وابن جريج والضحاك فعلى هذا يكون معناه اصبروا على طاعة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciprocal form صابروا suits the mutual contest of the combatants; ribāṭ similarly concerns two sides and preparing horses parallels the cited command to prepare force.
rows.anchor: لأن فاعل إنما يأتي لما يكون بين اثنين والرباط هو المرابطة

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muḥammad b. Kaʿb al-Quraẓī distinguishes endurance for one's religion, endurance of God's promises, and guarding against God's enemy.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd b. Aslam takes the command as persevering in jihad.
rows.anchor: أن المراد اصبروا على الجهاد عن زيد بن أسلم

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وجابر بن عبد الله وأبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: They explain ribāṭ as waiting for the prayers one after another, since frontier watch was not yet practiced at the time.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن معنى رابطوا أي رابطوا الصلوات ومعناه انتظروها واحدة بعد واحدة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says complete ablution in cold conditions, walking to congregational prayer, and waiting for one prayer after another constitute ribāṭ.
rows.anchor: إسباغ الوضوء في السبرات ونقل الأقدام إلى الجماعات وانتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر الباقر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir says endure misfortunes, persevere against your enemy, and guard against the enemy; this is close to the first interpretation.
rows.anchor: معناه اصبروا على المصائب وصابروا على عدوكم ورابطوا عدوكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands collectively cover duties, avoiding prohibitions, jihad against human and jinn adversaries and the self, defending Muslims and religion, then fearing God in all commands and prohibitions brings eternal success.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية تتضمن جميع ما يتناوله المكلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īnās means seeing and derives from the eye's pupil; in a reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh, أحستم means you perceived, by deletion of one doubled sīn.
rows.anchor: أخذ من إنسان العين وهو حدقتها التي تبصر بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isrāf is exceeding a permitted limit, usually by excess but sometimes through falling short; badārā means hastening and shares roots associated with fullness.
rows.anchor: وأصل الإسراف تجاوز الحد المباح إلى ما لم يبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the grammar, إسرافا and بدارا function as circumstantial verbal nouns, بالمعروف as a circumstantial phrase, and the bāʾ in بالله is extra so God is the subject of كفى.
rows.anchor: إسرافا مصدر وضع موضع الحال وكذلك قوله بدارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guardians must test orphans' understanding, religious uprightness, and financial judgment before handing over their assets.
rows.anchor: هذا خطاب لأولياء اليتامى أمرهم الله أن يختبروا عقول اليتامى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most commentators say reaching marriageable age means being able to have intercourse, not merely having a nocturnal emission, since some do not or late experience one.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد بالبلوغ الاحتلام لأن في الناس من لا يحتلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sounder view releases the orphan's property when maturity and sound judgment are both evident; his school defines puberty by fifteen years, puberty itself, or pubic hair.
rows.anchor: سلم إليه ماله وهو الأولى

rows.speaker: قتادة والسدي
rows.claim: Qatāda and al-Suddī explain sound judgment as intellect, religion, and uprightness.
rows.anchor: عقلا، ودينا، وصلاحا عن قتادة والسدي

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Ibn ʿAbbās take it as religious uprightness and sound management of property.
rows.anchor: صلاحا في الدين، وإصلاحا في المال عن الحسن وابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد والشعبي
rows.claim: Mujāhid and al-Shaʿbī say judgment means intellect alone, so even an old person is not given property if mentally unsound.
rows.anchor: عقلا عن مجاهد والشعبي قالا: لا يدفع إلى اليتيم ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The strongest definition combines intellect and competent financial management; a merely irreligious person may not be legally restrained if capable, while a financially destructive adult may be placed under guardianship.
rows.anchor: والأقوى أن يحمل على أن المراد به العقل وإصلاح المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Property may be delivered only after both puberty and sound judgment; guardians may not consume it beyond what God permits or hasten to spend before the orphan matures.
rows.anchor: وهو تعليق لجواز الدفع بالشرطين البلوغ وإيناس الرشد فلا يجوز الدفع قبلهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view permits a needy guardian to take only the amount needed for his work as a wage; the author prefers that reading over treating every use as excessive.
rows.anchor: فإن لولي اليتيم أن يتناول من ماله قدر القوت إذا كان محتاجا

rows.speaker: محمد بن مسلم
rows.claim: Muḥammad b. Muslim reports permission for a guardian tending an orphan's livestock to drink its milk without overmilking or harming the young.
rows.anchor: سألته عن رجل بيده ماشية لابن أخ له يتيم في حجره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rich guardian must take nothing from the orphan; a poor guardian may take an adequate amount by way of a loan and repay it when able, according to one reported view.
rows.anchor: من كان فقيرا فليأخذ من مال اليتيم قدر الحاجة والكفاية على جهة القرض

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وأبو العالية والزهري وعبيدة السلماني
rows.claim: These authorities report that a poor guardian may take from the orphan by way of a loan and repay it when able; this is also related from al-Bāqir.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وأبي العالية والزهري وعبيدة السلماني

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح وقتادة وجماعة
rows.claim: They say the poor guardian may take enough to end hunger and cover nakedness, but not as a loan; the school reports instead allow fair market wages, even above subsistence.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء بن أبي رباح وقتادة وجماعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās permits a guardian caring for an orphan's camels to use their milk without harming the offspring or overmilking them.
rows.anchor: وسئل ابن عباس عن ولي يتيم له إبل هل له أن يصيب من ألبانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When returning assets after maturity, guardians should have witnesses to protect themselves from denial or suspicion; God is sufficient witness and accountant.
rows.anchor: فاحتاطوا لأنفسكم بالإشهاد عليهم كي لا يقع منهم جحود
